T-001.label: Count usable stored pages
T-001.plain: Count available page text for documented and unclear institutions, and check storage capacity. These counts determine how much the back-fill must fetch again.

T-002.label: Measure cost and runtime
T-002.plain: Measure classifier and extractor calls, token use, runtime and link growth on a small sample. The results inform the paid-run budget and operating limits.

T-003.label: Calibrate supporting quote checks
T-003.plain: Test how well the quote matcher accepts genuine matches and rejects false ones across languages. Simone approves its settings and the website quote display limit.

T-010.label: Sign the shared codebook
T-010.plain: Prepare the codebook and generated contract wording for Simone's signature. The signed file fixes the coding rules and their release version.

T-011.label: Generate classifier question sets
T-011.plain: Build versioned page, activity and consolidation questions from the signed codebook. Preserve the approved wording and the order of questions and conditions.

T-012.label: Update schemas and constants
T-012.plain: Update generated field definitions, allowed values and version metadata, with compatibility checks for earlier formats. Assign each affected file to its owning task.

T-013.label: Build codebook generation tools
T-013.plain: Build the schema, loader and generators that turn the signed codebook into questions, prompts and documentation. Automated checks detect changes that break agreement with the codebook.

T-014.label: Keep page context and links
T-014.plain: Store page headers, footers and other surrounding text separately from the main text, along with web and email links. Newly fetched pages supply this context for contact details and follow-up searches.

T-015.label: Code source level fields
T-015.plain: Code each source's type, credibility, date, language and other source details. Use the shared rules for provenance and uncertainty.

T-016.label: Recheck revised questionnaire items
T-016.plain: Run a small paid pilot of the revised questions before relying on their wording. Simone runs the command and rules on the results.

T-020.label: Split and combine pages
T-020.plain: Split long pages to fit the classifier's token limit. Combine their answers using each codebook item's rule and retain the originating chunk.

T-021.label: Classify each source page
T-021.plain: Run the first classifier pass on each page in the approved question order. Record answers and confidence, and identify pages needing further evidence.

T-022.label: Extract page quotes and spans
T-022.plain: Extract verbatim support, activity spans and permitted text fields from source pages, and select follow-up links. Quote extraction follows the codebook's rules for keeping answers hidden.

T-023.label: Classify activities within pages
T-023.plain: Code each activity using its marked span within the source page. Apply the signed questions, activity conditions and round order.

T-032.label: Extract activity supporting text
T-032.plain: Extract verbatim support for positive or substantive activity codes. Keep each quote tied to the page chunk that produced the code.

T-024.label: Check support and confidence
T-024.plain: Check quotes against their source text and test whether they support the coded value. Apply the approved confidence and downgrade rules between coding rounds.

T-025.label: Follow missing evidence links
T-025.plain: Fetch selected links from incomplete pages within the hop and URL limits. Record how each source was found and when a limit or failure prevents further fetching.

T-026.label: Consolidate evidence and verdicts
T-026.plain: Combine page and activity records under the signed relationship and verdict rules. Preserve unresolved relationships and record the evidence behind each institution result.

T-027.label: Record automated coding answers
T-027.plain: Record each automated answer with its available probabilities, request details, question version and run setup. When a classifier omits the chosen-answer probability, preserve the returned code and omission in provenance, apply the existing downgrade rules and record the cause.

T-028.label: Write the new output rows
T-028.plain: Write the published fields, full supporting quotes and version metadata to CSV. Preserve the agreed handling of legacy fields, source text and support status.

T-030.label: Integrate the new run
T-030.plain: Connect the new coding stages to the pipeline's orchestration and configuration. Verify the new-run path with simulated service responses.

T-029.label: Build the back-fill command
T-029.plain: Reclassify a fixed institution list from all stored pages of each latest run, fetching pages again where required. Give every institution a recorded outcome under a fresh release identifier.

T-034.label: Correct transferred activity ownership
T-034.plain: Code the 114 reviewed transfer activities under their 45 verified owners. Keep corrections linked to the original observations without adding search records or changing denominators.

T-035.label: Integrate all processing paths
T-035.plain: Integrate the back-fill and ownership-transfer paths with the new-run pipeline. Check all three paths and regenerate the approved version records once.

T-031.label: Review the integrated implementation
T-031.plain: An independent reviewer checks the integrated code and contract against the specification. The review covers new runs, back-fill and ownership transfers.

T-040.label: Build labelled test cases
T-040.plain: Create synthetic cases for pipeline mechanics and real-page cases for coding rules and verdicts. Simone labels and approves the real-page expectations.

T-041.label: Run paid integration checks
T-041.plain: Run the labelled cases through all processing paths, plus a small back-fill using real observation identifiers. Simone runs the paid command and rules on failures.

T-050.label: Agree the publication interface
T-050.plain: Specify the public fields and display rules for Colin. Check implementation conformance, obtain authorization to send, and secure Colin's acceptance.

T-051.label: Add the database structure
T-051.plain: Prepare reversible database changes for correction records, version metadata and new coding fields. Keep original observations intact and support the agreed publication interface.

T-052.label: Update ingestion and API
T-052.plain: Load the new output format and serve the agreed fields, history and full supporting text. Keep new rows hidden until release and refresh public aggregates.

T-053.label: Update the public website
T-053.plain: Display each institution's latest row with its version, applicable fields and supporting text. Apply the approved display rules for older rows and translated text.

T-054.label: Rehearse loading and rollback
T-054.plain: Test migration, loading, visibility and rollback on a disposable copy of the live database. Verify correction links and confirm that original values remain unchanged.

T-055.label: Prepare the live backend
T-055.plain: Apply the reviewed database changes and deploy ingestion before the new pipeline goes live. Check that old runs still publish and new-format rows remain hidden.

T-060.label: Coordinate the procurement update
T-060.plain: Prepare the shared-codebook changes for the procurement integrator and obtain the required acceptance before deployment. Simone approves the message and the changes to that sibling plan.

T-061.label: Notify the validation owner
T-061.plain: Tell the validation integrator which contract and version inputs change and when. Obtain acknowledgement and a statement on whether the changes break locked inputs.

T-062.label: Coordinate AI-text adoption
T-062.plain: Prepare the AI-text-detection handoff for adoption of the shared codebook after deployment. Send it only after Simone approves the text.

T-063.label: Request calendar conversion rules
T-063.plain: Prepare a request to the multilingual subproject for calendar and fiscal-year conversion rules and shared language coverage. Simone approves the message before it is sent.

T-071.label: Deploy the revised pipeline
T-071.plain: Merge and deploy the reviewed pipeline after wave 5 is published and the required gates pass. Check the deployed version, credentials and available storage.

T-070.label: Freeze the back-fill population
T-070.plain: Fix the institution list at the approved freeze date. Include documented and unclear institutions plus the verified owners of transferred activities.

T-072.label: Test a small back-fill
T-072.plain: Run a varied sample through the back-fill and inspect its correction files. Use the results to project full-run cost and runtime for Simone's review.

T-073.label: Run the full back-fill
T-073.plain: Process the frozen institution set and record a result or named failure for each institution. Report progress and cost by batch.

T-074.label: Load and reconcile corrections
T-074.plain: Load the back-fill under a fresh release identifier after taking a database snapshot. Keep the rows hidden and reconcile the loaded results and refreshed aggregates.

T-080.label: Draw the quality sample
T-080.plain: Draw 400 institutions across the agreed four groups, plus a separate transfer-owner sample. Select the second-reader subset and record the sampling seeds.

T-081.label: Read the sample independently
T-081.plain: Have agents read sampled source pages without seeing the pipeline's codes. Record page and institution verdicts with enough detail to trace each judgment.

T-082.label: Compile the quality evidence
T-082.plain: Compare independent reads with pipeline verdicts and assemble support, confidence and traceability checks. Report agreement as agreement and identify disagreements for Simone's audit.

T-083.label: Simone audits the results
T-083.plain: Simone reviews every disagreement and 25 randomly selected cases. Her signed audit is required before the release decision.

T-090.label: Document the revised methods
T-090.plain: Generate the data dictionary and update the methods note, version history and related documentation. Simone approves the public wording.

T-095.label: Approve and publish results
T-095.plain: After the audit, Simone decides whether to release the new data. Publish through the API and website and check the released outputs.

T-096.label: Check reproduction and traceability
T-096.plain: Rerun the documented pipeline for 20 sampled institutions against an approved agreement criterion. Trace published codes to their pages, quotes, requests and versions.

T-097.label: Maintain the governed plan
T-097.plain: Receive task reports, prepare changes for Simone and maintain approved plan updates and completion records. Check the next publication window before the current one expires.

D-001.label: Shared signed codebook release
D-001.plain: A machine-readable codebook holds the approved coding rules. Its generators produce matching questions, prompts, schemas and documentation.

D-002.label: Revised production pipeline
D-002.plain: A production pipeline produces the new codebook's output for future runs and back-fill. It implements the approved coding, support and provenance rules.

D-003.label: Reclassified historical observations
D-003.plain: A back-fill release reclassifies documented and unclear institutions. Corrections remain linked to the original observations.

D-004.label: Published versioned research data
D-004.plain: The database, API and website publish the new fields and supporting text with their codebook version. The website shows the latest institution row while the backend retains run history.

D-005.label: Quality evidence and audit
D-005.plain: A packet combines independent agent reads, confidence checks and Simone's audit. It supplies the evidence for the release decision.

D-006.label: Updated definitions and methods
D-006.plain: The generated data dictionary, contract history and methods note document the new fields and coding rules. They explain version differences and how evidence is handled.

D-007.label: API and website handoff
D-007.plain: An interface specification tells Colin which fields and versions to publish and how to display mixed versions. It covers supporting text, source labels and the agreed privacy and translation rules.

D-008.label: Procurement codebook adoption
D-008.plain: A handoff coordinates the procurement pipeline's adoption of the shared codebook for its covered items. Changes to that locked plan require Simone's ruling there.

D-009.label: AI-text codebook adoption
D-009.plain: A handoff coordinates the AI-text pipeline's move to a pinned shared-codebook release after deployment. It identifies the affected cue and pilot specifications.

D-010.label: Calendar rule coordination
D-010.plain: A handoff asks the multilingual subproject for the calendar and fiscal-year conversion rules the pipeline needs. It also records ownership of shared language coverage.

RS-001.label: Project asset registry
RS-001.plain: The native writer's inventory records project assets and their locations. It is a reference for finding existing work.

RS-002.label: Approved plan and rulings
RS-002.plain: The planning files hold the approved specification, interview decisions and review record. They define the scope for this work.

RS-003.label: Unclear screening handoff
RS-003.plain: The earlier screening handoff records rulings, verified counts and the new-field footprint. It supplies inputs to the reclassification plan.

RS-004.label: Stored page counting scripts
RS-004.plain: Existing scripts enumerate stored runs, count pages and repeat the unclear-screen pilot. They provide a starting point for availability and sizing checks.

RS-005.label: Unclear screening pilot results
RS-005.plain: Stored counts and pilot answers describe the unclear set and its sampled pages. They provide evidence for planning and test-case selection.

RS-006.label: Remote institution screening records
RS-006.plain: Remote scratch records identify each institution's latest run and text or ambiguity flags. Their continued availability needs verification.

RS-007.label: Remote stored pages and outputs
RS-007.plain: The pipeline's stored page text and final CSVs are the inputs for historical reclassification. Reading them requires authorized server access.

RS-008.label: Local stored page corpus
RS-008.plain: A local copy of one run's scraped pages supports offline checks. It supplies source text without a fresh scrape.

RS-009.label: Earlier classifier comparison corpus
RS-009.plain: The earlier comparison package contains page archives and classifier agreement results. It supports offline testing and comparison without establishing accuracy.

RS-010.label: Current contracts and schemas
RS-010.plain: The existing production contracts, schemas and version checks define the starting format. Changes to their coding rules require Simone's approval.

RS-011.label: Earlier evidence review implementation
RS-011.plain: The archived implementation contains prior coding rules, quote checks and test cases. It serves as a reference for the revised pipeline.

RS-012.label: Classifier client and runner
RS-012.plain: The existing classifier client exposes answer confidence, probabilities and request metadata. The stage runner supplies the current integration pattern.

RS-013.label: Existing classification stage code
RS-013.plain: Current classification stages write answer metadata to institution files. They provide precedents for question versioning and classifier records.

RS-014.label: Existing validation stage code
RS-014.plain: The current validation stage includes page splitting and answer handling. Its missing metadata and split limitations identify work for the replacement.

RS-015.label: Existing extraction client code
RS-015.plain: The current extraction and batch modules implement the older model path. The new extractor requires an Anthropic client and revised extraction behavior.

RS-016.label: Existing scraping and fetching
RS-016.plain: Current scraper modules handle fetching, rendering and page parsing. Their treatment of surrounding text and links defines the changes needed for follow-up evidence.

RS-017.label: Existing pipeline orchestration code
RS-017.plain: The current orchestration code controls runs, sampling and resume behavior. It is the starting point for a fixed-list back-fill entry.

RS-018.label: Current output and documentation
RS-018.plain: The CSV writer, schema and operational documents describe the existing output path. They need alignment with the revised codebook.

RS-019.label: Existing pipeline test suite
RS-019.plain: Current unit and integration tests provide a base for checking the revised pipeline. New cases are needed for the added coding and processing behavior.

RS-020.label: Current API backend code
RS-020.plain: The backend schema, ingestion tools and API implement the current publication format. They are the starting point for correction records and new public fields.

RS-021.label: Publication wave visibility rules
RS-021.plain: Wave-window configuration controls which ordinary runs are visible. The live window must be checked before relying on recorded dates.

RS-022.label: Current website publication surfaces
RS-022.plain: The institution and comparison pages, data access and vocabulary code form the website publication surfaces. Colin owns their updates.

RS-023.label: Existing public API contract
RS-023.plain: The existing contract and frontend tracker provide the starting point for Colin's handoff. The generated data dictionary becomes the source of published definitions.

RS-024.label: Archived index coding proposal
RS-024.plain: The signed earlier proposal and pilot preserve the history of index coding rules. Current wording comes from the re-signed codebook and signature record.

RS-025.label: Documented institution evidence sample
RS-025.plain: The documented-institution list and detail sample provide identifiers, institution characteristics and evidence counts. They support back-fill preparation and quality sampling.

RS-026.label: Reviewed activity ownership package
RS-026.plain: The review package contains the authoritative 114 transfer activities and their 45 verified owners. It supplies the ownership corrections for back-fill.

RS-027.label: Incomplete combined review record
RS-027.plain: The earlier review records show partial coverage and handoff notes. They document remaining review work without supplying a completed row comparison.

RS-028.label: Earlier attribution correction tools
RS-028.plain: Registered scripts describe a prior attribution-correction package. Their listed worktree is absent, so the resource remains unverified.

RS-029.label: Procurement pipeline and plan
RS-029.plain: The procurement pipeline and its locked plan define the sibling update needed for shared coding. Their integrator owns changes in that project.

RS-030.label: Live published database and API
RS-030.plain: The live backend serves published verdicts and coverage counts. Authorized read-only queries can establish the population at the freeze date.

RS-031.label: Classifier and extractor services
RS-031.plain: TypeSafe supplies the classifier and Anthropic supplies the extractor. Paid calls require the stated approval and Simone-run process.

RS-032.label: Wave five pipeline run
RS-032.plain: The named wave-five run is an external input to deployment timing. Its publication must be confirmed before the revised pipeline deploys.

RS-033.label: Locked validation project plan
RS-033.plain: The sibling validation plan relies on the current contract surface. Its owner must assess how the new release affects those locked inputs.

RS-034.label: Existing comparison and rehearsal tools
RS-034.plain: Run comparison and database rehearsal utilities provide existing patterns for checks. They can support verification of the revised outputs and loading process.

RS-035.label: Retired pilot test artifacts
RS-035.plain: Earlier test runs and pilot data are retained as historical resources. The plan bars them from use as evidence.

RS-036.label: Harvested unclear institution sample
RS-036.plain: The public-API harvest records the unclear population and an 800-institution detail sample. It supplies population counts and evidence characteristics for planning.

RS-037.label: Anthropic extractor access
RS-037.plain: The project's Anthropic organization and key provide extractor access. Deployment and rate-limit checks remain assigned to their respective tasks.

RS-038.label: AI-text pipeline and specifications
RS-038.plain: The AI-text repository contains the cue and pilot specifications targeted by the shared-codebook handoff. Its owner controls changes there.

RS-039.label: Codebook review and rulings
RS-039.plain: The first two codebook review rounds and Simone's recorded replies supply the settled item choices. They are inputs to the signed codebook.

RS-040.label: Multilingual pipeline ownership
RS-040.plain: The multilingual subproject owns the shared calendar-conversion rule and language coverage. The handoff requests the rules needed by the year method.
